## Natural history notes

A slender meadow katydid characterized by a narrow green to brownish body, long antennae, thin legs, and a delicate cone-shaped head typical of meadow katydids. In Florida, the Graceful Meadow Katydid is found in grassy wetlands, marsh edges, wet prairies, ditches, fields, pine flatwoods, and other open habitats with tall grasses, sedges, and low vegetation. It feeds mainly on grasses, seeds, and tender plant material, sometimes taking tiny insects, while males call from vegetation and the species serves as prey for birds, spiders, frogs, and other insect-eating animals.
